prompt: Why doesn't the brain just spiral into endless bliss the moment it feels something good? Write a short blog post on that puzzle, and bring in whatever you know about advanced meditation.

I just lost a day at work to a bug caused by Ruby's Timeout. Write a blog post explaining how Timeout works under the hood, why it's dangerous, and how other languages have dealt with the same idea of killing a thread from the outside.

I know almost nothing about the technical side, but I've been following the AI risk debate. Do the recent advances in neural networks change how we should think about superintelligent AI as a goal-maximizing agent? Write an exploratory essay.
Write about a teacher who changed your life in only a few lessons. I want to give it to some of my students and their parents.

You've built a research career without an undergrad degree or a PhD, and teenagers keep emailing to ask whether they should skip university. Write the essay you wish you could send them: how to think about the decision, and the costs and pressures that come with not going, including the ones nobody warns you about.

Why do horoscope-style personality descriptions feel so uncannily accurate? I'd like a short essay that goes beyond 'they're vague' and asks what it would mean if those statements are true of almost everyone, and what we could learn from that.
Why is coming up with genuinely new ideas so hard, and why do so many of them show up in dreams or by accident? Write a short, speculative blog post.

I've been reading Bostrom's Superintelligence and got stuck on the idea of a hyper-competitive Malthusian future full of digital agents where consciousness might get optimized away. Write something speculative about whether anything meaningful could survive in that kind of economy, and where it might hide.

I have a five-year-old and I keep wondering how I'll ever explain the internet to her, and honestly how I should be using it myself. Write a thoughtful blog post on using the internet well, as something you get better at over time rather than something that just happens to you.

I just got back from a talk on effective charity where one of the speakers argued that donors are mostly fooling themselves. Write me a blog post about what it's like to hear that, and whether the idea of investing your money now and giving it away later actually holds up. Do some back-of-the-envelope math.

Perf review season is coming and I have to write peer reviews for coworkers I think are great. Everything I write comes out as 'X is awesome, love working with them.' Can you write a blog post on how to write positive feedback in a review that's actually useful to the person and to their managers?

I want a book-review style blog post about the Baumol effect as an explanation for why health care and education keep getting more expensive. Lay out the case, then say honestly what still bothers you.
Write a manifesto for someone who wants to live entirely in the future: always chasing what's newest and next. Make the case sincerely, as if you believed it.
Udemy vs Skillshare, Uber vs Lyft: the same teachers, drivers and customers use all of them. Write up some thinking on what peer-to-peer businesses end up looking like once they reach scale.

Everyone seems to read the Great Filter as proof that humanity is doomed. Write an essay on whether that's right: which candidate explanations for the Fermi paradox actually hold up, and how scared should we be?

Write an exploratory blog post, from the point of view of an engineer at a tech company, about the open questions you have about open source: when to use it versus building your own, why companies pay people to write it, and how you're supposed to evaluate it. It's fine to raise more questions than you answer.

I just finished a book about Soviet economic planning and the mathematicians who tried to fix it. Write a long, thoughtful review that goes beyond the plot to what it teaches about planning, incentives and who ought to run a country.
Tech companies keep lobbying for easier immigration for programmers, and critics say we should just train more Americans instead. Write a short, punchy essay taking a side in that argument.
Write a practical piece on how to get real value out of attending a music industry conference, for someone who's about to go to their first one and tends to waste these things.

The New York Times just ran a piece on the Hearing Voices Movement, people with hallucinations who want them treated as normal rather than medicalized. You're a psychiatrist who has met some of them. Write a numbered-points blog post giving your honest, mixed take: where the movement has a point and where its critics (and the press coverage) do.
Write a blog post for startup founders about why automating every part of a business might be a mistake. Draw on your experience running an online store.

Is the placebo effect actually real? I keep hearing it's one of the most powerful forces in medicine, but I've also seen claims that it's overblown. Write up what the evidence really says and how you'd make sense of it.

I'm curious about applying evolutionary thinking to psychiatry, which seems like it should be a natural fit but rarely is. Write a thoughtful review of a book that tries it, covering what the theory is, how well it handles real psychiatric conditions, what it might mean for society, and where you stay skeptical.

You're a psychiatrist reflecting on your own habits. Write an essay on the two broad stances a doctor can take toward what patients say they want, taking them at their word versus looking for the real problem underneath, and which one you lean toward and why.

Is fixing every bug in your software actually the right goal? Write an essay for a small software company owner on how to decide which bugs are worth fixing, with practical ways to find out about them and put a number on it.

I've heard that gout is oddly common among famous, successful people, and that there might be a real biochemical reason for it. Write a skeptical but curious blog post on whether high uric acid could actually make you more accomplished.

Someone at a party told me that if a product could be better, a competitor would already have built the better version, so markets basically guarantee things work about as well as they can. That doesn't match my experience buying anything, as a consumer or as a company. Write an essay on why it's so hard to buy products and services that actually work well, and what that means for the build vs. buy decision.

I tried a Kaggle competition, landed nowhere near the leaderboard, and now I'm wondering if I'm just bad at machine learning. You do ML as your actual job. Can you write a blog post about how real-world machine learning work compares to Kaggle?

I keep seeing devs who just have the LLM write code and paste errors back to it until it works, without really thinking. Models are getting good enough that maybe that's fine? Is there any future where that approach actually pays off for them?
My mom says she raised me so I owe her everything, including taking care of her when she's old. How far does a debt like that actually go?
I sell my small software product both as a downloadable desktop app and as a web app. Is it actually worth keeping the desktop version around?
honest question: why do you think so few women want to join early-stage startups?
You run an accelerator that picks companies after a short interview. Why do funding rounds take months to close, and does it really have to be that way?
people always say 'greed is good' and it makes me cringe. is there any version of that claim that actually makes sense?
We're an early-stage startup and I honestly don't know what number we should be tracking or what 'good' looks like. How should we think about growth?
Two senior people on our open source project keep arguing about whether a section of the docs is clear. Each thinks their rewrite is better. How do you actually settle that kind of thing?
I just found out there are already a few companies doing basically what I want to build. Am I too late? Should I drop the idea?
if one country gets superintelligent AI a few months before its rival, why would that be dangerous? is there a historical analogy?
if I really can't model something, can't I just say I don't know and refuse to put a probability on it? like choosing between a safe grant and a wild long shot
Should a company care more about its customers than about its own survival?
what's the deal with over-abstracting things? why do clever people end up building vague 'general' systems that miss the point?
Should a small, very productive core team of a language like Julia slow down to add code review, tests and internal docs so outsiders can contribute more easily? Or is that not worth it?
how come people say anti-rape poster campaigns are proven effective? what's the evidence and is it any good?

Why does everyone complain about lag on tablets and VR headsets but nobody seems to care about keyboard-to-screen latency on a normal computer? Is keyboard input just inherently less sensitive to delay?
can you build a startup hub like Silicon Valley in another city, or is it a one-off? what would it actually take?
Do you think we actually understand deep learning yet, or is the field still pretty ad hoc? Write a few paragraphs on it.
How did Steven Pressfield finally manage to finish a book after years of calling himself a writer?
Why do some bloggers refuse to promote friends' projects? Explain it as if you were one of them.
I'm stuck in silver in Overwatch and everyone says you have to play DPS to climb out of low ranks. Is that actually true?
we can't match big-company salaries. what are some cheap ways to make employees feel valued and keep them from leaving?
Should I quit my job and start a company? I've been asking successful people for advice but it's all contradictory. Why?
Do you ever notice how your friend group doesn't look like the general population at all, even though you never chose it that way?
I feel completely unmotivated today, nothing seems worth doing. What should I do with a day like this?
Polls say a huge share of Americans would give a kidney to a stranger, yet almost nobody actually does. Why is the gap so enormous? Is everyone just lying?
Is the slippery slope argument ever a good reason to oppose something that seems reasonable on its own?
why are corporations so hard to regulate? they always seem to find a loophole
I've felt guilty for years about something I did when I was young. How reliable is my memory of it, really, and can I do anything about the past?
is there really that much money in US politics? how does it compare to other stuff we spend on
A VC wants to put a small check into our seed round. Someone warned me about 'signalling risk' if they don't follow on later. How worried should I be?
We've built something people clearly need but sales are slow. Should we just copy how the established competitors in our market sell?
When I don't know which product to buy I just ask someone who works in that field. That's the sensible approach, right?
how do I become more of an independent thinker instead of just absorbing the views I grew up with?
why do you build tolerance to heroin but people with ADHD can apparently stay on Adderall for years? that always seemed weird to me
Tim Berners-Lee's web won, but I keep feeling like we ended up with the wrong kind of internet. Is there a real case that the web is shaped badly, as opposed to just being the thing that happened?
why do so many startup founders fail, and what do the ones who succeed have in common?
ok be honest, what's the deal with On the Road? is it actually any good?
You've used Tailwind for years. Why switch to vanilla CSS now?
